Evaluating the spatio-temporal dynamics of low- and mid-trophic level resources in the Azores: implications for the new MPA network and cetacean populations

**Summary**
This study investigated the spatio-temporal distribution of low- and mid-trophic level biomass in the Azores using the SEPODYM-LMTL ecological model from 1998 to 2023. Three variables were analyzed: **net primary production (NPP)**, **zooplankton**, and **micronekton**. Areas were classified into three **productivity zones**: recurrent, occasional, and unfavorable. Productivity within the new **Marine Protected Area** (MPA) network was assessed to see if MPAs overlapped with highly productive waters. Inter-annual variability was high, with no overall trends in NPP or zooplankton biomass. Spatial distribution showed a strong latitudinal gradient, with high productivity near the islands and north of 37°N (Azores Counter Current). **Fully protected MPAs had higher productivity** from April to November, while highly protected areas were similar or lower than unprotected zones. **Baleen whales were mostly observed in occasional productivity zones**, particularly in July; no clear patterns emerged for dolphins or deep-diving species. These results provide a baseline for evaluating the ecological value of MPAs and suggest productivity zones may be important for higher trophic levels. Long-term monitoring and additional environmental predictors are needed to fully understand their significance.
------------------------------------------------------------------------ **Keywords** SEAPODYM-LMTL • trophic levels • productivity zones • marine protected areas • cetaceans ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Methods - Ecological model outputs from **SEAPODYM-LMTL** - Analysis of **three productivity indicators** - Net Primary Production (NPP)\ - Zooplankton biomass\ - Micronekton biomass - **Time series analysis** (1998–2023) - **Spatial analysis** of productivity hotspots - Classification of **productivity zones** - recurrent\ - occasional\ - unfavorable - Comparison with **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)** - **Cetacean sightings dataset** from the POPA program (2001–2015) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Key Results ::: {style="text-align: left;"} - **Strong spatial heterogeneity** in marine productivity across the Azores. ::: ![](files/Master_thesis/productivity.png){width="80%" style="display:block; margin:0 auto;"} ::: {style="text-align: left;"} - A **high-productivity region** was identified around the islands and **north of 37°N**. ::: ![](files/Master_thesis/productivity_zones.png){width="80%" style="display:block; margin:0 auto;"} ::: {style="text-align: left;"} - **Fully protected MPAs** tend to overlap with **more productive waters**, especially between **April and November**. ::: ![](files/Master_thesis/MPA_productivity.png){width="80%" style="display:block; margin:0 auto;"} ::: {style="text-align: left;"} - **Baleen whales** were more frequently observed in **occasional productivity zones**, particularly during summer. - No clear association was detected for **dolphins** and **deep-diving cetaceans**. ::: ![](files/Master_thesis/Cetaceans_productivity.png){width="80%" style="display:block; margin:0 auto;"}
